newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Yachting-America's Cup draws record 18 entries.
newsitem.headline: Yachting-America's Cup draws record 18 entries.

text.p: New Zealand received a record 18 entries from 10 countries to compete for yachting's most prestigious trophy, the America's Cup, before the deadline for entries to the 2000 challenge closed on Wednesday.
The United States, which has held the cup for almost all its 144 years, leads the charge with six challenges including an entry from four-time winner Dennis Conner.
France has three entries, Switzerland two, Italy, Australia, Britain, Japan, Russia, Hong Kong and Spain one each.
Some entrants are expected to drop out before racing begins but they had to pay a US$200,000 entry fee by Wednesday to be able to race in the 1999 challenger series.
The winner of that series challenges New Zealand the next year.
The leader of the 1995 New Zealand team which won the Cup from San Diego, Sir Peter Blake, said he was delighted with the level of entries.
One late dropout was Canada, he told Radio New Zealand.
"We think the majority are going to turn up. It's a terrific line-up."
Blake said he expected Japan would mount a very strong challenge as would one of the Swiss teams.
Defending the cup would be even tougher than winning it, he said.

"It's going to be even tougher in many ways, there's a lot more stress in it and the rest of the world is ganging up on New Zealand and they are going to try and rip our arms and legs off effectively," he said.
